quotes.text: Not everything that is faced can be changed, but nothing can be changed until it is faced.
quotes.author: James Baldwin*

quotes.text: The world always seems brighter when you've just made something that wasn't there before.
quotes.author: Neil Gaiman*

quotes.text: In the middle of every difficulty lies opportunity.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein*

quotes.text: If I lost this final, I maybe would have never won a Slam.
quotes.author: Alexander Zverev, Roland-Garros trophy ceremony, 7 June 2026* (fresh off the press, not a LinkedIn graphic in sight)

quotes.text: Freedom comes next.
quotes.author: Alexander Zverev, Roland-Garros, June 2026* (said after winning his first Grand Slam — earned, not recycled)

quotes.text: The world is not to be put in order; the world is order itself. It is for us to harmonize with it.
quotes.author: Henry Miller*

quotes.text: The pessimist complains about the wind; the optimist expects it to change; the realist adjusts the sails.
quotes.author: William Arthur Ward*

quotes.text: Do not wait to strike till the iron is hot; but make it hot by striking.
quotes.author: William Butler Yeats*

quotes.text: Knowing trees, I understand the meaning of patience. Knowing grass, I can appreciate persistence.
quotes.author: Hal Borland*

quotes.text: The future belongs to those who believe in the beauty of their dreams.
quotes.author: Eleanor Roosevelt*

quotes.text: Not the load, but how you carry it.
quotes.author: Lena Horne* (said it once, meant it always)

quotes.text: In theory, theory and practice are the same. In practice, they are not.
quotes.author: Yogi Berra*

quotes.text: I am not afraid of storms, for I am learning how to sail my ship.
quotes.author: Louisa May Alcott*

quotes.text: It is only when we are no longer fearful that we begin to create.
quotes.author: J.M.W. Turner*

quotes.text: The most common form of despair is not being who you are.
quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard*

quotes.text: Luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity.
quotes.author: Seneca*

quotes.text: The man who moves a mountain begins by carrying away small stones.
quotes.author: Confucius*

quotes.text: The universe is under no obligation to make sense to you.
quotes.author: Neil deGrasse Tyson*

quotes.text: Doubt is not a pleasant condition, but certainty is absurd.
quotes.author: Voltaire*

quotes.text: Tell me, what is it you plan to do with your one wild and precious life?
quotes.author: Mary Oliver*

quotes.text: All changes, even the most longed for, have their melancholy; for what we leave behind us is a part of ourselves.
quotes.author: Anatole France*

quotes.text: We don't see things as they are, we see them as we are.
quotes.author: Anaïs Nin*

quotes.text: The question is not what you look at, but what you see.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau*

quotes.text: Act as if what you do makes a difference. It does.
quotes.author: William James*

quotes.text: A year from now you may wish you had started today.
quotes.author: Karen Lamb*

jokes.text:
I tried to write a joke about sustainability, but all my good material was recycled.

---
Wednesday, 03 June 2026

I tried to come up with a joke about time — but I didn't want to waste yours.

---
Thursday, 04 June 2026

I used to be indecisive. Now I'm not so sure.

---
Saturday, 06 June 2026

I signed up for a gardening club. The membership fees were steep, but the perks really grew on me.

---
Sunday, 07 June 2026

I tried to organise a surprise party for my calendar. It didn't work — it already knew all the dates.

---
Tuesday, 09 June 2026

I tried to make a reservation at the library. They were fully booked.

---
Wednesday, 10 June 2026

I tried to start a business selling calendars. It only lasted a year.

---
Monday, 22 June 2026

I tried to win an argument with a calendar. It had too many dates on me.

---
Wednesday, 24 June
I started a business selling

I told my boss it was my first day and I was nervous. He said, "Don't worry — just be yourself." I've never felt less prepared.

---
Thursday, 02 July 2026

I tried to watch the F1 race without making a noise. I just couldn't keep a straight face.

---
Sunday, 05 July 2026

I tried to read a book about the ocean. I got totally lost at C.

---
Saturday, 11 July 2026
I entered a pun contest. I submitted ten entries hoping one would win. No pun in ten did.

I tried to come up with a joke about contracts. But I couldn't get the terms right.

---
Thursday, 16 July 2026

I tried to organise my weekend — but it had other plans.

---
Friday, 17 July 2026

I went to a restaurant and asked for something that would impress my girlfriend. They handed me the bill.

---
Saturday, 18 July 2026

I told someone I was reading a book about anti-gravity. They asked if it was good. I said I couldn't put it down.

---
Sunday, 19 July 2026

I told my calendar I needed a day off. It said every single day was already booked — by me.

---
Monday, 20 July 2026

I told someone I was learning about neurosymbolic AI. They asked if it was complicated. I said it depends on how you look at it — which is, unfortunately, also the answer.

---
Tuesday, 21 July 2026

I told someone I was writing a thoughtpiece about AI. They asked if it was long. I said it depends — am I counting the words, or the existential crises?

---
Wednesday, 22 July 2026

I told someone I was looking into getting a UK driver's licence. They said, "How hard can it be?" I said I'd let them know — once I figure out which side of the form to fill in.

---
Thursday, 23 July

I tried to plan a relaxing Cotswolds weekend. Ended up with a twelve-point itinerary, a quarterly photo series, and a LinkedIn draft due at noon.

---
Friday, 24 July 2026

I tried to relax in the countryside. Turned out I'd brought a twelve-point itinerary, a boot full of terracotta, and a quarterly photo obligation. Close enough.

---
Saturday, 25 July 2026

I booked a quiet weekend in the countryside to escape my to-do list. Turns out my to-do list had already checked in.

---
Sunday, 26 July 2026

I tried to write a joke about Mondays. It kept pushing itself to Thursday.

---
Monday, 27 July 2026

I tried to explain carbon insetting to someone at a dinner party. They nodded politely for six minutes and then asked if I wanted more bread.

---
Tuesday, 28 July 2026

I tried to organise a blood donation. Turns out the whole thing was a bit draining.

---
Wednesday, 29 July 2026

I tried to come up with a concept for a new app. My AI assistant loved the idea and said it was already building it.

---
Thursday, 30 July 2026

I asked my Friday to be more productive. It said it was already fully booked — doing nothing at pace.

---
*Friday, 31 July 2026*

I tried to take a day off from being productive. It went well — I'd scheduled it in three weeks ago and had a four-point checklist ready.

---

keepInMindHistory.item: **Yankees trade deadline is Monday (Aug 3):** With Judge out since May 31 and Bellinger injured, the next 48 hours of Yankee moves will matter. Keep half an eye on it for family chat with Ted and Teddy.

**Community Shield is two weeks away (16 Aug, Cardiff):** Arsenal vs Man City — Arsenal qualified as 2025–26 Premier League champions, City as FA Cup winners. Worth keeping an eye on whether you want to watch with anyone. The transfer window is also swinging hard — Bruno Guimaraes saga is moving fast.

**August = second half of the year, month one:** Good moment to revisit any personal or Cedara goals you set for the year. The cotinus check this morning is a useful metaphor — some things recover slowly, and that's fine, as long as you're logging it.
